Let \(D\) denote a dark square and \(W\) a white square. The original board is

\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
W&D&W&W&W\\
W&D&W&W&W\\
W&D&D&W&W\\
W&D&W&W&D\\
W&W&W&D&D
\end{array}
\]

A \(270^\circ\) clockwise turn is equivalent to a \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise turn. Thus, the columns of the original board, read from right to left, become the rows of the rotated board:

\[
\begin{array}{ccccc}
W&W&W&D&D\\
W&W&W&W&D\\
W&W&D&W&W\\
D&D&D&D&W\\
W&W&W&W&W
\end{array}
\]

This pattern matches Board E.

\[

\]
